Westbury Advisors curates an exclusive portfolio of luxury residences, expertly acquiring, transforming, furnishing, and managing each property with meticulous attention to detail.

The holdings shown here are selected.

Selected Properties

54 Second Avenue

East Village 1901

A row house between Third and Fourth Streets, built 1901. Three apartments. The East Village before it acquired the name.

678 Ninth Avenue

Hell's Kitchen 1925

Corner of Forty-Seventh and Ninth, built 1925. The building sat through every version of Hell's Kitchen — rough, then overlooked, then expensive. Seven apartments.

236 West 10th Street

West Village 1905

Between Bleecker and Hudson on West Tenth, built 1905. Thirty-three apartments on a block that has become one of the harder ones to leave.

133 West 25th Street

Chelsea 1921

Between Sixth and Seventh on Twenty-Fifth, built 1921. Nineteen apartments at a corner that has been called Chelsea, NoMad, and Midtown South in the last twenty years. The building predates all three.

376 Bleecker Street

West Village 1852

Between Charles and Perry on Bleecker, built 1852. Three apartments above the street. The structure was here before the neighborhood had its current name, or most of its current character.
